primary.title: The Work of Marconi
primary.author: Guglielmo Marconi
primary.rationale: This is a foundational text outlining Marconi's early work and vision for wireless telegraphy. It's likely to be found in collections of his writings or speeches.

primary.title: Radio-Telegraphy: Its Theory and Practice
primary.author: Guglielmo Marconi
primary.rationale: A significant publication detailing the technical aspects and practical applications of his inventions, likely preserved in scientific journals or collected works.

primary.title: Nobel Lecture
primary.author: Guglielmo Marconi
primary.rationale: Marconi's Nobel Prize lecture would be a key primary source, detailing his achievements and their significance. Such lectures are often published and archived.

secondary.title: Marconi: The Man Who Invented the World
secondary.author: Marcello Pelosi
secondary.rationale: A recent scholarly biography offering a comprehensive look at Marconi's life and work, likely drawing on extensive archival research.

secondary.title: The Invention of Radio
secondary.author: Charles P. Bright
secondary.rationale: This academic book provides historical context for the development of radio, with significant attention to Marconi's contributions and the scientific landscape of the era.

secondary.title: Guglielmo Marconi: A Biography
secondary.author: W. J. Baker
secondary.rationale: While slightly before 1976, this is a highly regarded and comprehensive biography that remains a standard scholarly work on Marconi. It's often cited in later research.

suggestions.notes: Primary source availability on Wikisource and Project Gutenberg for Marconi's specific writings might be limited. Internet Archive is a more probable repository for his published works and speeches. The secondary source by W. J. Baker is included as a foundational scholarly work, though it predates the 1976 cutoff.
